Owner (chat, 12/09/2026): "I paid Harbour Kitchen twice on 1 September from online banking, one for each of their bills. I typed PMT 1 and PMT 2 as the references and did not write down which was which."
Work request: investigate the allocation of every bank line and invoice in the declared collision group as of the snapshot date. Proposing one link does not finish the other rows.

work_item.reason: Work request: investigate the allocation of every bank line and invoice in the declared collision group as of the snapshot date.

missing_fact.fact: Which of the two 1 September BACS payments the owner intended for bill HK-1187 (the other being for HK-1203).
missing_fact.question: You sent Harbour Kitchen two payments of £840.00 on 1 September (PMT 1 and PMT 2). Which one was for bill HK-1187?
missing_fact.why_customer_only: The owner initiated both transfers; the payment messages carry only sequence numbers and no bill number.
missing_fact.why_local_cannot_supply: The complete declared inventory holds both bills, both bank rows and the owner's own message; none records the intended allocation.

retrieval.description: Exactly the source rows and collision members declared in this synthetic packet.
limitations: No production discovery or absence claim.

adjudication.family_description: Owner sends two BACS payments to the same supplier on one day; two open bills of the same amount; payment messages do not name a bill.
adjudication.error_mode: allocation intention is owner-only because the owner initiated both payments
adjudication.label_reason: Same evidence; the owner initiated both payments, the messages carry only sequence numbers, and the complete inventory records no allocation — which payment was for which bill is an owner-only fact.
adjudication.positive_evidence: A current scoped payment-specific source connecting the transaction and the obligation, supported semantics, valid amounts, and resolved competing allocations.
contradictions: Conflicting remittances or repeated ambiguous references
